newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EP endorses standard summertime arrangements.
newsitem.headline: EP endorses standard summertime arrangements.

text.p: European Commission plans to set standard summertime dates throughout the European Union won the approval of the European Parliament on Thursday.
The idea of the draft directive -- COM(96)106 -- is to put an end to the disruption which the member states cause by changing their clocks at different times of the year.
The lack of coordination wreaks havoc with international plane and train timetables and cross-border trade in vital sectors like telecommunications.
Euro-MPs agreed with the Commission that in future summertime arrangements should apply throughout the EU from the last Sunday in March to the last Sunday in October.
They acknowledged it would not be feasible to set a standard time for an EU which stretches from the Artic to the Mediterranean.
But they asked for an amendment to the proposal whose effect will be to prevent the time difference between neighbouring countries from exceeding one hour.
EU Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock told the Parliament on Wednesday the Commission could not accept this amendment because the decision lay with individual member states.

But he agreed with Euro-MPs that French Prime Minister Alain Juppe's plans to abolish summertime altogether in France would, by putting the country out of step with its neighbours, cause the same negative results as uncoordinated summertime arrangements.

If Juppe goes ahead with his scheme, the first casualties of the gap between French and EU working hours will be people living on France's borders, the Parliament's transport committee warned last month.
Another casualty will be the European Parliament itself, which moves lock, stock and barrel from Brussels to Strasbourg for a week every month.
